description: Project AstroCadet is an immersive aerospace simulation program designed to train the next generation of space exploration personnel. Operating within high-fidelity simulated environments, the Junior Astronaut Training Team (J.A.T.T.) conducts integrated flight operations, spacecraft telemetry monitoring, and extravehicular orbital scenarios.The initiative bridges foundational STEM education, operational spaceflight methodology, emphasizing real-time problem solving, crew resource management.
summary:
ASTRAHEALTH AI is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring and decision-support prototype designed to support health monitoring during space missions. Using NASA's Inspiration4 Whole Blood Measurements dataset, the system analyzes astronaut health observations to identify unusual patterns that may require further review.

The platform combines a PyTorch-based Autoencoder and an Isolation Forest model for exploratory anomaly detection. A rule-based monitoring agent transforms model outputs into structured monitoring priorities, maintains execution history, and supports human-in-the-loop review and approval.

Through an interactive dashboard, mission teams can explore health observations, analytics, anomaly flags, and decision-support insights in one place.

ASTRAHEALTH AI demonstrates how machine learning can assist astronaut health monitoring and support informed human review during future space missions. It is a research prototype, not a clinically validated diagnostic system.
details:
ASTRAHEALTH AI — Detailed Project Description

1. Overview

ASTRAHEALTH AI is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring and decision-support research prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It explores how machine learning can help identify unusual patterns in astronaut health observations and organize them into structured monitoring priorities.

2. Problem and Motivation

Human spaceflight exposes astronauts to challenging environments that can affect their health. Monitoring health observations over time and identifying unusual patterns are important for supporting mission teams. ASTRAHEALTH AI aims to demonstrate a data-driven approach that helps organize health information and highlight observations that may require further human review.

3. How the System Works

The system uses NASA's Inspiration4 Whole Blood Measurements dataset from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR-569).

The data pipeline performs feature preparation, missing-value handling, and scaling before passing observations to the machine learning models.

Two complementary anomaly-detection approaches are implemented:

  • PyTorch Autoencoder: Learns a compressed representation of health measurements and uses reconstruction error to flag unusual observations.
  • Isolation Forest: Identifies observations that differ from patterns in the dataset.

The model outputs are processed by an experimental rule-based risk-scoring engine. A monitoring agent organizes the results into monitoring priorities and supports a human-in-the-loop approval workflow.

4. Main Features

  • Astronaut health monitoring dashboard.
  • Health analytics and observation exploration.
  • Machine-learning-based anomaly detection.
  • Experimental monitoring priority scoring.
  • Agent-based decision-support workflow.
  • Human approval and rejection controls.
  • Persistent monitoring execution history.
  • AI health assistant interface.

5. Technology Stack

  • Programming: Python
  • Deep Learning: PyTorch
  • Machine Learning: Scikit-learn
  • Data Processing: Pandas, NumPy
  • Visualization and Interface: Streamlit
  • Computer Science Tools: Git and GitHub
  • Storage: SQLite

6. Current Prototype Evidence

The current implementation processes 27 retained observations from four Inspiration4 participants, using 18 model input dimensions, including missingness indicators.

The software includes two anomaly-detection models and a rule-based monitoring agent. Its automated test suite contains 26 passing tests, verifying core software functionality.

These results demonstrate prototype functionality, not clinical performance or diagnostic accuracy.

7. Limitations and Future Scope

The dataset is small and does not contain verified clinical anomaly labels. Therefore, the model outputs are exploratory anomaly flags and must not be interpreted as medical diagnoses or validated health-risk predictions.

Future work could include larger astronaut health datasets, expert-reviewed labels, additional physiological measurements, stronger validation, and integration with mission-relevant monitoring systems.

8. Expected Impact

ASTRAHEALTH AI demonstrates a potential approach for combining machine learning, health-data analytics, and human review into a unified astronaut monitoring workflow. Its long-term goal is to explore how intelligent decision-support tools could assist mission teams in understanding astronaut health observations during future space exploration.

Disclaimer: ASTRAHEALTH AI is a research prototype and is not clinically validated or intended for medical diagnosis or treatment.
